To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the standard perturbative result for the static QCD potential gets corrections of the order of Λ2/Q2; (b) the running coupling α s (Q 2 ) freezes in the infrared; (c) the exchanged gluon has an effective tachionic mass; (d) the infrared sensitivity of the perturbative potential is removed after resummation of all the corrections.

(1) The standard result for the potential between two heavy quarks gets corrections of order (Λ/Q2)2, both at small and intermediate momentum transfers Q2; (2) After resummation, the running coupling α(Q2) freezes to a constant in the infrared, α(0) = 0.5; (3) The exchanged gluons acquire an effective mass, m2 = −Λ2, which is tachyonic; (4) The potential
the static potential between two quarks in QED and QCD is given by the standard expression, except for the fact that the running coupling freezes in the infrared.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the infrared behavior of QCD.
the infrared behavior of the static potential in QCD.
the calculation of the potential between a heavy quark and antiquark in perturbative QCD with modified boundary conditions, i.e., we add an infrared sea of soft gluons to the perturbative states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the standard perturbative result for the potential in QCD is modified in a way that is consistent with confinement.
the static potential between two static color sources is not a gauge invariant quantity.
the infrared sensitive corrections to the static potential are large and should be taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the static potential in QCD is modified in a non-trivial way by the infrared physics of the theory.
the standard static potential is a good description of the potential between two heavy quarks only at large momentum transfers Q≫Λ, but not at small Q.
the infrared sensitive corrections to the static potential are of the same order as the corrections from the perturbative running coupling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the infrared sensitivity of the static potential is a consequence of the perturbative series being divergent.
the infrared behavior of the running coupling is not universal, and depends on the choice of asymptotic states.
the standard perturbative potential is not a good approximation to the full nonperturbative potential.
